validity.recommendation: no change to existence/classification/attribution; row is a real, correctly-classified, correctly-attributed FERC-jurisdictional interstate transmission project (Columbia Gas Transmission / TC Energy, FERC docket CP18-137). See separate spec concern on LengthKnown.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed by 6 independent sources of 3 different classes -- an EIA govt data article, an FERC-order trade-press article (S&P Global Platts, naming docket CP18-137), an operator trade-press placed-in-service notice (North American Oil & Gas Pipelines), a conservation-NGO federal-intervention press release (Center for Biological Diversity, May 2018, filed a motion to intervene in the FERC docket), a local-news wire story on the FERC environmental assessment comment period (Ohio News Connection via Cleveland Scene, June 2019), and a pre-filing trade-publication planned-projects listing (Pipeline News, rev 7/2018). None of these trace to GEM or to each other -- none cites GEM, and the FERC-docket coverage (S&P Global, CBD, Ohio News Connection) is independent of the completion coverage (EIA, NA Pipelines). CLASSIFICATION: correct -- this is FERC's own characterization (an interstate natural-gas transmission certificate, CP18-137) of a pipeline-replacement/looping/compression project on Columbia Gas Transmission's R-System, not a gathering or processing line. DUPLICATE: checked against the 46-row roster -- no other row is 'Buckeye' or plausibly the same physical pipe; nearest name-cluster risk is the unrelated 'Mountaineer' collision (P0221 vs P0307/P2040), which does not touch this project. Confirmed distinct from Leach XPress (P0209) and Mountaineer XPress (P0221), which are separate, differently-docketed TC Energy/Columbia projects that Buckeye Xpress's new 36-in pipe was built to diameter-match (per S&P Global). ATTRIBUTION: Owner1=TC Energy 100% confirmed (S&P Global: 'according to parent company TC Energy'; NA Pipelines: 'TC Energy's U.S. Natural Gas team ... placing into service its Buckeye XPress (BXP) project'; CBD, May 2018, pre-2019-rebrand: 'owned by TransCanada Corp.'). StartState/Province=Ohio and EndState/Province=West Virginia confirmed by both S&P Global/FERC order and the Pipeline News PDF, which enumerate the exact same county list (Vinton, Jackson, Gallia, Lawrence counties OH; Wayne County WV) -- GEM records only the start county (Vinton) and end county (Wayne), which is a valid subset (segment start/end convention) but does not capture Jackson/Gallia/Lawrence; noting for completeness, not contesting (StartState/Province and EndState/Province themselves are correct). One local-news source (Ohio News Connection, June 2019) says the route goes 'under the Ohio River into Kentucky' -- this conflicts with the FERC order's own county list and is very likely the reporter conflating the physical new pipe (OH+WV only, per FERC) with the downstream capacity destination (CGT's interconnection at Leach, Kentucky, per EIA) -- not treated as a state-column concern given the primary FERC-derived source is unambiguous and more precise. Opened 8 of 8 harvested wiki citations for this row; 6 were citable and used (EIA todayinenergy id=47156, S&P Global Platts via Wayback, NA Pipelines via Wayback, Center for Biological Diversity, Ohio News Connection/Cleveland Scene, Pipeline News PN1018 PDF); 2 excluded as generic navigation surfaces that never name this pipeline (eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php and the FracTracker map homepage -- both checked, neither contains the word 'Buckeye').

validity.recommendation: correct LengthKnown from 64.00 mi to ~66 mi (FERC order states 66.1 mi of new pipe precisely)
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's LengthKnown=64.00 mi traces to a single, PRE-FILING planning estimate: the Pipeline News PN1018 PDF (data as of its 'REV 7/18' revision, i.e. mid-2018, before the project's final FERC application/order) lists 'Length: 64 miles' for the Buckeye Xpress Project. Every source that postdates FERC's environmental review and final order gives a different, internally consistent figure: the Center for Biological Diversity's May 2018 press release (filed at the same early stage) already says 'the proposed 66-mile fracked-gas pipeline'; the FERC order itself (via S&P Global Platts, Jan 2020) states precisely 'Buckeye XPress entails replacement of 60.8 miles of 20- and 24-inch-diameter pipeline with about 66.1 miles of new 36-inch-diameter pipeline'; Ohio News Connection (June 2019, reporting on FERC's environmental assessment) says '66 miles of 36-inch natural-gas pipeline to replace a 20-inch pipeline'; EIA's todayinenergy completions article (March 2021, post-construction) says the project 'replaced 66 miles of existing natural gas pipeline with more reliable 36-inch pipe.' That is 4 independent sources spanning 2018-2021 agreeing on ~66 (66.1) miles of new pipe, against 1 single-origin planning-stage estimate of 64. GEM's LengthKnown column tracks built/replaced pipe length, so 66.1 (the FERC order's own precise figure for the new 36-in pipe) is the better-supported value; 64 appears to be a stale pre-application estimate that never got updated after the docket (CP18-137) reached its final scope. Not silently overwritten -- flagged here for the paste-surface, candidate value 66.10 mi.
